What a /13 means

A /13 holds 524,288 addresses. Blocks this size are regional or provider aggregates and are always subdivided before use.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /13 uses 13 network bits and leaves 19 host bits, so the block contains 524,288 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−13) − 2 = 524,288 − 2 = 524,286.

Configuration examples

interface Vlan10
 ip address 10.0.0.1 255.248.0.0
!
access-list 10 permit 10.0.0.0 0.7.255.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.0.1/13

Linux

ip addr add 10.0.0.1/13 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /13?

524,286. A /13 has 524,288 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 524,286 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /13?

255.248.0.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.7.255.255.
